html:
Our Build Process for Custom Sprinter Van Conversions

Every Abroga Vans conversion follows a four-phase build process designed to deliver off-grid capability, engineering precision, and complete transparency. From initial CAD layout to final handoff with comprehensive documentation, we treat each Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and Ford Transit conversion as a bespoke engineering project, not a furniture installation.

Our process makes sure that every electrical system, plumbing manifold, and cabinet assembly is specified and documented before you take delivery. Whether you're planning a minimalist weekender or a full-time basecamp, understanding how we build helps you make informed decisions about timeline, budget, and customization.

Phase 1: Consult & CAD Layout

The foundation of every conversion is a custom 3D layout design tailored to how you actually travel. During the consultation phase, we map your power budget, spatial requirements, and off-grid priorities to create a detailed CAD rendering of your interior.

This phase includes component selection for your electrical system, from lithium battery bank sizing to inverter specifications, and establishes the footprint for cabinetry, plumbing, and climate systems. The CAD layout serves as the blueprint for procurement and fabrication, and final pricing is locked after this phase is complete.

We provide power budget analysis to ensure your solar array, battery capacity, and inverter output align with your actual electrical loads, whether you're running a 12V fridge or adding induction cooking and a microwave.

Phase 2: Component Sourcing

Once the layout is approved, we buy wholesale appliances and solar components at builder pricing. A build can include marine-grade electrical components like Xantrex inverters and Outback chargers, lithium battery banks, and pre-loomed wiring harnesses built for continuous off-grid use.

Component sourcing also covers plumbing (fresh and gray water tanks and filtered water manifolds), climate control, and cabinetry hardware designed to withstand long-term vibration and road stress. A build can include a sealed diesel heater such as a Webasto or Espar unit.

By sourcing components directly, we maintain quality control and ensure compatibility across all systems. Lead times for specialty items like custom solar arrays or specific inverter models are communicated during this phase.

Phase 3: Precision Build & Fabrication

The build phase includes professional fabrication, electrical wiring drop-ins, and finish carpentry. Every conversion receives four-season insulation, mass-loaded sound deadening (on applicable tiers), and furniture-grade cabinetry with weight-optimized framing.

Electrical systems are installed with pre-loomed harnesses, labeled circuits, and accessible service points. Plumbing is winterized for year-round travel, and all penetrations are sealed to prevent water intrusion. We provide weekly photo updates so you can track progress from framing to final assembly.

Phase 4: Handoff & Walkthrough

At delivery, you receive in-person system training covering electrical operation, plumbing maintenance, climate controls, and troubleshooting. We walk through every switch, breaker, fuse panel, and service point so you understand how to operate and maintain your systems on the road.

You also receive comprehensive as-built documentation including wiring diagrams, component specifications, and maintenance schedules. This documentation is critical for future repairs, upgrades, or resale.

Our handoff process ensures you're confident operating your van's systems before you leave the shop. We answer questions about battery management, inverter settings, water filtration, and heater operation until you're fully comfortable.

What to Expect: Timeline & Communication

Build timelines depend on current queue availability and component lead times. We take a limited number of conversions per year to ensure every chassis receives full shop attention and quality control.

After submitting a build request, you'll receive a response within two business days. Qualified builds include a free power budget review, and no deposit is required to receive a scoped estimate.

During the build, expect weekly photo updates and direct communication for any design adjustments or component substitutions. Transparency is built into every phase, from initial pricing to final walkthrough.

Choosing Your Build Tier

Abroga Vans offers three transparent build tiers, each with defined scope and pricing. All tiers include bespoke layout design, marine-grade electrical systems, and professional cabinetry.

The Weekender starts at $20,000 and includes a 250Ah lithium battery bank, solar array with shore power hookup, premium insulation, roof ventilation, custom kitchen galley, 12V fridge, and hand-crafted cabinet storage. This tier suits minimalists, weekend warriors, and climbers.

The Explorer starts at $25,000 and adds a 500Ah battery upgrade, integrated plumbing (cold water sink with fresh and gray tanks), single burner induction cooktop, mass-loaded sound deadening, and DC-DC alternator charging. This tier suits off-grid campers seeking self-sufficiency.

The Basecamp starts at $35,000 and includes a 750Ah battery bank, hot water system routed to sink and shower, and custom indoor wet bath. A build can include a Webasto or Espar cabin heater. This tier is designed for full-timers and luxury travelers.

Estimates reflect typical scope on a 144" wheelbase chassis. Final pricing is locked after the CAD layout phase. View detailed specifications and add-ons on our pricing page.

Engineering Standards & Safety

Electrical systems use marine-grade components chosen for daily off-grid use.

We use smart lithium battery banks with integrated battery management systems and pre-loomed wiring harnesses with proper gauge sizing and circuit protection. Plumbing systems are winterized, and all diesel heaters are sealed and vented to prevent carbon monoxide intrusion.

Cabinetry is built with commercial hardware and weight-optimized framing to stay tight after hundreds of thousands of miles. We don't build furniture. We build equipment designed for the long haul.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a custom Sprinter van conversion take?

Build timelines vary based on current queue availability and component lead times. After your CAD layout is approved and components are sourced, the precision build and fabrication phase typically takes several weeks. We provide weekly photo updates and communicate any delays due to specialty component availability.

Do I need to own a van before starting the process?

No. If you don't own a Mercedes Sprinter, Ford Transit, or RAM Promaster yet, we can help you search for the right van for your build. You buy the van yourself. During the intake process, you'll indicate whether you own a van or need help searching for one, and we'll guide you on wheelbase, roof height, and drivetrain options.

What's included in the as-built documentation?

At handoff, you receive comprehensive documentation including wiring diagrams with labeled circuits, component specifications and model numbers, maintenance schedules for batteries and plumbing, and troubleshooting guides. This documentation is essential for future service, upgrades, or resale.

Can I add custom features beyond the three build tiers?

Yes. The three tiers provide transparent starting points, but every conversion is bespoke. Common add-ons include roof-mount AC units with battery upgrades, outdoor showers, composting or cassette toilets, DC-DC alternator charging, backup cameras, and added windows. Custom requirements are captured in the intake form and priced during the CAD layout phase.

What makes Abroga Vans different from other conversion builders?

We engineer systems like equipment, not furniture. Abroga uses marine-grade electrical components, professional cabinetry with commercial hardware, and winterized plumbing built for four-season travel. A build can include Xantrex inverters and Outback chargers. We provide comprehensive as-built documentation, in-person system training, and transparent pricing locked after CAD layout, so there are no surprise costs at delivery.

Ready to Start Your Custom Conversion?

We take a limited number of conversions per year to ensure every chassis receives full shop attention. Tell us about your project and we'll follow up with a scoped estimate, power budget review, and current queue availability.

Start Your Build Request

Response within two business days. No deposit required to receive an estimate.
